Galicia has a very mild climate for its latitude due to the marine influence.
Galicia experiences exceptionally mild winters with consistently heavy rainfall.
Snow is rare in Galicia due to temperatures rarely dropping below freezing.
The warmest coastal station of Pontevedra has a yearly mean temperature of 14.8 °C (58.6 °F).
Ourense, located somewhat inland, is only slightly warmer with 14.9 °C (58.8 °F).
Galicia's climate is still very cool by Spanish standards due to its exposed north-westerly location.
In coastal areas of Galicia, summers are tempered, averaging around 25 °C (77 °F) in Vigo.
In inland areas of Galicia, such as Ourense, days above 30 °C (86 °F) are very regular.
The warmest day of the year (1971–2000) will achieve a temperature of 26.6 °C (80 °F), although in June 1976 the temperature reached 31.6 °C (89 °F), the site record.
On average, 4.25 days of the year will report a maximum temperature of 25.1 °C (77 °F) or above.
During the winter half of the year, the coldest night will typically fall to −4.1 °C (25 °F).
Typically, 18.6 nights of the year will register an air frost.

Seattle experiences frequent rain in autumn, winter, and early spring.
Winters in Seattle are cool and wet, with December being the coolest month.
Summers in Seattle are sunny, dry, and warm, with August being the warmest month.
The hottest officially recorded temperature in Seattle was 103 °F (39 °C) on July 29, 2009.
The coldest recorded temperature in Seattle was 0 °F (−18 °C) on January 31, 1950.
The record cold daily maximum in Seattle was 16 °F (−9 °C) on January 14, 1950.
The record warm daily minimum in Seattle was 71 °F (22 °C) on the day the official record high was set.
The average window for freezing temperatures in Seattle is November 16 thru March 10, allowing a growing season of 250 days.

Delhi: Delhi features a dry-winter humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cwa) bordering a hot semi-arid climate (Köppen BSh).
Delhi: The warm season lasts from 21 March to 15 June with an average daily high temperature above 39 °C (102 °F).
Delhi: The hottest day of the year is 22 May, with an average high of 40 °C (104 °F) and low of 28 °C (82 °F).
Delhi: The cold season lasts from 26 November to 9 February with an average daily high temperature below 20 °C (68 °F).
Delhi: The coldest day of the year is 4 January, with an average low of 2 °C (36 °F) and high of 14 °C (57 °F).
Delhi: In early March, the wind direction changes from north-westerly to south-westerly.
Delhi: From April to October the weather is hot.
Delhi: The monsoon arrives at the end of June, along with an increase in humidity.

Delhi: The brief, mild winter starts in late November, peaks in January and heavy fog often occurs.Temperatures in Delhi usually range from 2 to 47 °C (35.6 to 116.6 °F), with the lowest and highest temperatures ever recorded being −2.2 and 48.4 °C (28.0 and 119.1 °F), respectively.
Delhi: The annual mean temperature is 25 °C (77 °F); monthly mean temperatures range from 13 to 32 °C (55 to 90 °F).
Delhi: The highest temperature recorded in July was 45 °C (113 °F) in 1931.
Delhi: The average annual rainfall is approximately 886 mm (34.9 in), most of which falls during the monsoon in July and August.
Delhi: The average date of the advent of monsoon winds in Delhi is 29 June.

Claus von Stauffenberg: Stauffenberg's full name was Claus Philipp Maria Justinian, followed by the noble title of "Count of Stauffenberg".
Claus von Stauffenberg: He was born in the Stauffenberg castle of Jettingen between Ulm and Augsburg, in the eastern part of Swabia, at that time in the Kingdom of Bavaria, part of the German Empire.

Claus von Stauffenberg: Schenk (i.e., cupbearer/butler) was an additional hereditary noble title.
Claus von Stauffenberg: The ancestral castle of the nobility was the last part of the title, which was Schenk Graf von Stauffenberg and used as part of the name.
Claus von Stauffenberg: The Stauffenberg family is one of the oldest and most distinguished aristocratic Catholic families of southern Germany.

Claus von Stauffenberg: Among his maternal Protestant ancestors were several famous Prussians, including Field Marshal August von Gneisenau.On 11 November 1919, a new constitutional law, as part of the Weimar Republic, abolished the privileges of nobility.

Claus von Stauffenberg: Article 109 also stated, "Legal privileges or disadvantages based on birth or social standing are to be abolished. Noble titles form part of the name only; noble titles may not be granted any more."

Because of their rising military and economic power, the warriors ultimately became a new force in the politics of the court.
Their involvement in the Hōgen in the late Heian period consolidated their power, and finally pitted the rival Minamoto and Taira clans against each other in the Heiji Rebellion of 1160.

Houston's land surface is underpinned by unconsolidated clays, clay shales, and poorly cemented sands up to several miles deep.
The region's geology developed from river deposits formed from the erosion of the Rocky Mountains.
These sediments consist of a series of sands and clays deposited on decaying organic marine matter, that over time, transformed into oil and natural gas.
Beneath the layers of sediment is a water-deposited layer of halite, a rock salt.
As it pushed upward, the salt dragged surrounding sediments into salt dome formations, often trapping oil and gas that seeped from the surrounding porous sands.

At times when a death sentence is affirmed on direct review, it is considered final.
Yet, supplemental methods to attack the judgment, though less familiar than a typical appeal, do remain.
These supplemental remedies are considered collateral review, that is, an avenue for upsetting judgments that have become otherwise final.
Where the prisoner received his death sentence in a state-level trial, as is usually the case, the first step in collateral review is state collateral review.
(If the case is a federal death penalty case, it proceeds immediately from direct review to federal habeas corpus.)
Although all states have some type of collateral review, the process varies widely from state to state.
The purpose of these collateral proceedings is to permit the prisoner to challenge his sentence on grounds that could not have been raised reasonably at trial or on direct review.

records.text: The Grand Canal was restored under the Yongle Emperor's rule from 1411 -- 1415

Shipping the annual 4,000,000 shi (one shi is equal to 107 liters) was made difficult with an inefficient system of shipping grain through the East China Sea or by several different inland canals that necessitated the transferring of grain onto several different barge types in the process, including shallow and deep - water barges
William Atwell quotes Ming dynasty sources that state the amount of collected tax grain was actually 30 million shi (93 million bushels), much larger than what Brook notes
The Yongle Emperor commissioned some 165,000 workers to dredge the canal bed in western Shandong and built a series of fifteen canal locks
The reopening of the Grand Canal had implications for Nanjing as well, as it was surpassed by the well - positioned city of Suzhou as the paramount commercial center of China

Despite greater efficiency, there were still factors which the government could not control that limited the transportation of taxed grain; for example, in 1420 a widespread crop failure and poor harvest dramatically reduced the tax grain delivered to the central government

Political status of Puerto Rico is that of an unincorporated territory of the United States.
As such, the island is neither a sovereign nation nor a U.S. state.
Because of that ambiguity, the territory, as a polity, lacks certain rights but enjoys certain benefits that other polities have or lack.
For instance, in contrast to sovereign nations, Puerto Rico does not have voting rights in its federal legislature nor in electing its federal head of government.
But, in contrast to U.S. states, Puerto Ricans are not subject to federal income taxes.
The political status of the island thus stems from how different Puerto Rico is politically from sovereign nations and from U.S. states.

Hemostasis is the body's instinctive response to stop bleeding and loss of blood.
Vascular spasm is the first response in the hemostatic process, where blood vessels constrict to allow less blood to be lost.
Platelet plug formation is the second step in the hemostatic process, where platelets stick together to form a temporary seal over the break in the vessel wall.
Coagulation or blood clotting is the third and last step in the hemostatic process, where fibrin threads reinforce the platelet plug.
Platelets are a large factor in the hemostatic process, allowing for the creation of the platelet plug that forms almost directly after a blood vessel has been ruptured.

Sweating sickness first came to the attention of physicians at the beginning of the reign of Henry VII in 1485.
The disease broke out on 19 September 1485; it had killed several thousand people by its conclusion in late October that year.

It was regarded as being quite distinct from the Black Death, the pestilential fever, or other epidemics previously known because of the sweating which gave it its name and its extremely rapid and fatal course.
It reached Ireland in 1492, when the Annals of Ulster record the death of James Fleming, 7th Baron Slane from the pláigh allais, newly come to Ireland.

The Annals of Connacht also record this obituary, and the Annals of the Four Masters record 'an unusual plague in Meath' of 24 hours' duration; people recovered if they survived it beyond that 24-hour period.

records.text: War on Terror: On the morning of 11 September 2001, 19 men affiliated with al-Qaeda hijacked four airliners all bound for California.

War on Terror: The hijackers – members of al-Qaeda's Hamburg cell – intentionally crashed two airliners into the Twin Towers of the World Trade Center in New York City.
War on Terror: Both buildings collapsed within two hours from fire damage related to the crashes, destroying nearby buildings and damaging others.

War on Terror: The hijackers crashed a third airliner into the Pentagon in Arlington County, Virginia, just outside Washington D.C. The fourth plane crashed into a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania, after some of its passengers and flight crew attempted to retake control of the plane, which the hijackers had redirected toward Washington D.C., to target the White House, or the U.S. Capitol.

There are 69 known moons of Jupiter.
This gives Jupiter the largest number of moons with reasonably stable orbits of any planet in the Solar System.

The most massive of the moons are the four Galilean moons, which were independently discovered in 1610 by Galileo Galilei and Simon Marius and were the first objects found to orbit a body that was neither Earth nor the Sun.
From the end of the 19th century, dozens of much smaller Jovian moons have been discovered and have received the names of lovers or daughters of the Roman god Jupiter or his Greek equivalent Zeus.

Heliocentrism is the astronomical model in which the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun at the center of the Solar System
Historically, Heliocentrism was opposed to geocentrism, which placed the Earth at the center
The notion that the Earth revolves around the Sun had been proposed as early as the 3rd century BC by Aristarchus of Samos
in the medieval world, Aristarchus's Heliocentrism attracted little attention -- possibly because of the loss of scientific works of the Hellenistic Era
Astronomers maintained a geocentric world view for many thousands of years.
Most believed Earth was stationary at the center of the Universe and categorically different from the divine or ethereal objects that moved through the sky.
Aristarchus of Samos speculated on a heliocentric reordering of the cosmos.
Nicolaus Copernicus developed a mathematically predictive heliocentric system in the 16th century.
Galileo Galilei, Johannes Kepler, and Isaac Newton developed a modern understanding of physics in the 17th century.

The investigation of geological phenomena such as mountains and craters and seasonal meteorological phenomena such as clouds, dust storms, and ice caps on the other planets led to the acceptance of the idea that Earth moves around the Sun and that the planets are governed by the same physical laws that govern Earth.

Oganesson: Oganesson is a synthetic chemical element with the symbol Og and atomic number 118.
Oganesson: It was first synthesized in 2002 at the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research (JINR) in Dubna, near Moscow in Russia, by a joint team of Russian and American scientists.
Oganesson: In December 2015, it was recognized as one of four new elements by the Joint Working Party of the international scientific bodies IUPAC and IUPAP.
Oganesson: It was formally named on 28 November 2016.

Oganesson: The name is in line with the tradition of honoring a scientist, in this case the nuclear physicist Yuri Oganessian, who has played a leading role in the discovery of the heaviest elements in the periodic table.

Oganesson: It is one of only two elements named after a person who was alive at the time of naming, the other being seaborgium; it is also the only element whose namesake is alive today.Oganesson has the highest atomic number and highest atomic mass of all known elements.
Oganesson: The radioactive oganesson atom is very unstable, and since 2005, only five (possibly six) atoms of the nuclide 294Og have been detected.

Oganesson: Although this allowed very little experimental characterization of its properties and possible compounds, theoretical calculations have resulted in many predictions, including some surprising ones.

While the mainland coasts of Greece and Turkey bordering the Aegean Sea on both sides represent roughly equal shares of its total coastline, the overwhelming number of the many Aegean islands belong to Greece.
In particular, there is a chain of Greek islands lined up along the Turkish west coast (Lesbos, Chios, Samos, and the Dodecanese islands), partly in very close proximity to the mainland.
Their existence blocks Turkey from extending any of its zones of influence beyond a few nautical miles off its coastline.

records.text: Under Charlemagne the Franks reached the height of their power.

The Carolingian Empire was a conscious effort to recreate a central administration modeled on that of the Roman Empire.
Charlemagne hoped to provide his nobles an incentive to fight by encouraging looting on campaign.
Plunder and spoils of war were stronger temptations than imperial expansion, and several regions were invaded over and over in order to bolster the coffers of Frankish nobility.

records.text: North Carolina - National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Grant Program: # North Carolina - National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Grant Program ***created_at*** : 2024-06-21 00:00:00 ***updated_at*** : 2024-06-21 14:06:39 ***state** : North Carolina **implementing sector***: State ***program category*** : Financial Incentive ***program type*** : Grant Program ***sector*** : Commercial ***start date*** : 2022-10-01 04:00:00 ***end date** : 2026-09-30 04:00:00 ***administrator*** : North Carolina Department of Transportation ***funding Source*** : Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) ***budget*** : $109,024,196 ***Incentive Amount*** : Varies, grants are awarded competitively ***Maximum Incentive*** : Varies, grants are awarded competitively ***Equipment Requirements*** : Projects must meet the standards established by [23 CFR Part 680](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-02-28/pdf/2023-03500.pdf) ***Installation Requirements*** : Projects must meet the standards established by [23 CFR Part 680](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2023-02-28/pdf/2023-03500.pdf) ## Summary : **_Note:[The Federal Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA)](https://www.congress.gov/117/plaws/publ58/PLAW-117publ58.pdf#page=993) created the [National Electric Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) Formula Grant Program](https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/environment/nevi/) with a total budget of $5 billion.

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: # 4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review: Hancock software, which is approved by DOE for the state’s WAP and LIHEAP programs, will be built out to help implement the HEAR program.

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: This software system is used by the CAP auditors who visit a home to complete a pre-home assessment that will determine if a household is eligible for a program (e.g., WAP, LIHEAP, 50122 rebate).

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: If an auditor determines a household is eligible for the HEAR program after completing the pre-home assessment, they will work with the homeowner or building owner and renter to apply for the HEAR program.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: Household can also apply directly through OER’s website instead of through a CAP through an application portal built out by Hancock.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: Hancock Software will use automation to identify missing information or errors in the application.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: Once applications are submitted, they will be flagged for manual review by OER.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: All the application data will be collected and stored on the Hancock Software platform including information on the pre and post home assessment.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The address of the household where an eligible installation occurred will be collected in the pre and post home assessment.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The address collected in the pre and post home assessment will be cross referenced to ensure it matches the address on the rebate coupon.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The home address will be stored in the client’s file on Hancock to maintain a record of the addresses that have received the HEAR program rebate.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The project scope will also be reviewed to verify consistency with program requirements.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: If discrepancies are found in the project scope, they will be addressed and resolved by OER or the CAPs.

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: For households served by the CAPs, categorical income eligibility through WAP, LIHEAP, or Public Housing documentation can be verified using the Hancock software.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The CAPs have WAP, LIHEAP, and Public Housing enrollment data from the RI Department of Human Services (DHS).

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: For households that submit income forms through the Hancock application portal such as their 1040, W-2, or four consecutive weeks of pay stubs, OER will review and manually approve these submitted forms.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The Hancock Software will organize applications based on the household income of the applicant.

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: If an applicant does not meet the low- or moderate-income threshold, then they will be notified though email that they are not eligible for the rebate based on the program’s income requirements.

4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: In the ${\mathsf{C A P s^{\prime}}}$ post home assessment, the auditor will check the completed work with the contractor's invoice and HEAR program requirements.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: The invoice and post assessment information will be stored in the client’s file on Hancock.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: OER will also randomly sample invoice costs every quarter to compare contractor costs.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: If a contractor’s costs are consistently higher than others, OER will issue a warning and provide them with an opportunity to substantiate their costs.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: If the contractor continues to charge significantly more, they will be removed from the qualified contractor list.
4.1 Hancock Software for Data Review:: All records will be maintained on Hancock software.

Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): # Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal) ***created_at*** : 2022-08-18 00:00:00 ***updated_at*** : 2022-08-18 00:00:00 ***state** : Federal **implementing sector***: Federal ***program category*** : Financial Incentive ***program type*** : Personal Tax Credit ***sector*** : Residential, Multifamily Residential, Low Income Residential ***Incentive Amount*** : 30% ***Maximum Incentive*** : $1,000 ## Summary : **_Note: Section 13404 of The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 ([H.R. 5376](https://www.congress.gov/117/bills/hr5376/BILLS-117hr5376enr.pdf#page=149)) modified and extended the expiration date for the Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Credit.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): The summary below described the credit as modified by H.R. 5376.

Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): _** Qualified alternative fuel vehicle refueling equipment not subject to depreciation allowances, including electric vehicle charging equipment, is eligible for a tax credit of 30% up to $1,000.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): These projects do not have to meet the same labor standards as commercial projects in order to qualify for the full 30% tax credit.

Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): Section 13801 of The Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 also established procedures for other parties to monetize certain tax credits, including this one, for equipment placed in service on or after January 1, 2023 and through December 31, 2032.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): The _direct pay_ option allows non-taxable entities to directly monetize certain tax credits.

Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): The provisions apply to nonprofits, a state or political subdivision thereof, the Tennessee Valley Authority, Indian tribal governments (as defined in Section 30D(g)(9)), any Alaska Native Corporation (as defined in Section 3 of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act), or any corporation operating on a cooperative basis which is engaged in furnishing electric energy to persons in rural areas.

Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): Such applicable entities can elect to be treated as having made a tax payment equal to the value of the tax credit they would otherwise be eligible to claim.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): The entity can then claim a refund for the excess taxes they are deemed to have paid.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): The option effectively makes this tax credit refundable for these entities.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): The act also allows eligible taxpayers to _transfer_ all or a portion of their eligible tax credits to an unrelated taxpayer.
Alternative Fuel Vehicle Refueling Property Tax Credit (Personal): Transfers must be reported to IRS and only one transfer is permitted.

Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: # Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure # Nevada's Alternative Fueling Infrastructure Plan for Electric Vehicle Infrastructure # Overview As a result of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA) National Electrical Vehicle Infrastructure (NEVI) program, over the next five years, the Nevada Department of Transportation will receive $\$38$ million to support publicly accessible electric vehicle (EV) charging.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: The goal of this program is to create a national network of charging stations.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: The NDOT Alternative Fueling Infrastructure Plan, also known as the NDOT NEVI plan, is Nevada's plan to spend this $\$38$ million.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: # How Federal Funding Will Be Used Under the NEVI guidelines, initial funding prioritizes interstate highways.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: Interstate Highways are designated as Alternative Fuel Corridors (AFC).
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: The goal for Nevada is to achieve “Fully Built-Out” status along these AFCs.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: With some exceptions, this generally means that travelers can expect to find a fast-charging station every 50 miles in close proximity to the interstate.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: The list below illustrates the specific NEVI requirements.

Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: # Phase 1 NEVI Station Criteria One mile from the highway 50 miles between stations DC fast charging stations with at least four ports with CCS connector Power output of at least 150kW per port After completing work on the AFC's, NDOT will enter into the next phase of prioritization and funding will be available for more locations and purposes.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: # Timeline On September 14, 2022, the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) approved the Nevada Electric Vehicle Infrastructure Deployment Plan (available here).

Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: For the first year of funding (FY 2023), NDOT focused on coordinating with NV Energy and Wells Rural Electric to deploy EV infrastructure along the state's Alternative Fuel Corridors in their service territories.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: On September 29, 2023, FHWA approved NDOT's Plan Update for FY 2024 (available here).
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: For the second year (FY 2024), NDOT will continue its partnership with NV Energy and rural electric companies to advance the proposed sites along interstates.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: Other potential sites along Alternative Fuel Corridors will also be identified.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: More details on the site selection process can be found here.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: On November 15, 2024, FHWA approved NDOT's Plan Update for FY 2025,these plan updates can be viewed here.

Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: With a focus on collaboration and coordination to serve all of Nevada with a data-driven approach to planning, this plan will be updated annually through FY 2027.
Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: To learn more about the basics of EV charging, click here!

Electric Vehicle (EV) Infrastructure: This Charging and Fueling Infrastructure Discretionary Grant Program (CFI) is a competitive grant program to strategically deploy publicly accessible electric vehicle charging and alternative https://www.dot.nv.gov/mobility/alternative-fueling-infrastructure-plan 2/6 fueling infrastructure in the places people live and work.

policy 22736: • Turn down water heater set points to reduce energy usage in making domestic hot water.
policy 22736: • Block EVs from charging, or allow EVs to charge at a reduced power level 0 rate (in lieu of standard 32A level 2 rate).
policy 22736: • Utilize home batteries to supply load to the Customer's home or inject power into the utility system.
policy 22736: • Peak Events are anticipated to occur no more than 5 times per month for an average of 3 to 4 hours at a time.
policy 22736: The Customer will be sent notification of a Peak Event, via a smartphone app or other electronic method.

The Energy Infrastructure Revolving Loan Program (EIRLP) was enacted in the 2021 Iowa legislative session and is administered by the Iowa Energy Center (IEC) within the Iowa Economic Development Authority (IEDA).
The EIRLP administrative rules can be found in Iowa Administrative Code section 261.406.
The program can provide loans for the development and construction of energy infrastructure.

Energy infrastructure is defined in Iowa Code as 'land, buildings, physical plant and equipment, and services directly related to the development of projects used for, or useful for, electricity or gas generation, transmission, storage or distribution.'

policy 22420: This handbook does not replace administrative rules or Iowa Code regarding the EIRLP.

The BPU has not provided any quantitative analysis of the economic impact of the Proposed Rule because the majority of the costs and impacts have already been accounted for in previous rulemaking proceedings.
The Proposed Rule creates several categories of costs that would presumptively be paid by non-participating ratepayers.

The BPU’s Economic Impact statement is also deficient because it does not consider the potential impact of the Proposed Rule on the State’s ability to meet its overall renewable energy goals within the cost caps established in the Clean Energy Act.

Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: Following the closure of the current solar renewable energy certificate (SREC) program to new applicants, existing “legacy” projects will continue to receive SRECs for the remainder of their 15-year SREC eligibility period.
Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: The cost cap must accommodate both the costs of compensating legacy projects for their SRECs and the costs of new renewable energy development.

Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: At current retail sales levels and SREC prices, the funds needed to cover the cost of SRECs generated by legacy projects will meet, or even exceed the Clean Energy Act cost cap.

Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: Thus, the BPU must reduce the amounts paid for SRECs from legacy projects to create a budget for the costs of new renewable energy initiatives that will affect utility rates during and after Energy Year 2022.
Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: The additional costs for community solar that are contemplated in the Proposed Rule will be included in that budget.

Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: A quantification of those costs is essential in order to establish the budget for the Pilot Program and permanent community solar programs, and the economic impact of the Proposed Rule.

Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: The commenter notes also that the BPU has not supported the statement that one of the costs of the Pilot Program, the net metering credit, “has been selected based on reasonable and prudent estimates of the cost of community solar project development.”

Notice of Proposal Impact Statements: The Proposed Rule contains no analysis of the “cost of community solar project development” nor the level of the net metering credit required to cover such costs.

P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: # P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE In Docket No. 23-08-02, Annual Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review - Year 3, the Authority conducted discovery on the issue of solar panel waste to determine whether proactive steps were needed before solar panel waste becomes a prevalent issue in Connecticut.

P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: The Authority determined that waste may potentially become a problem in the NRES, SCEF, and ESS Programs, in addition to the RRES Program, once commercial solar and batteries reach their end of life.

P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: Consequently, the Authority requested that CGB work in consultation with relevant stakeholders, including DEEP and the EDCs, to develop recommendations to resolve the issue of solar panel and battery recycling and waste for clean energy projects in Connecticut.
P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: RRES Decision, pp. 51-52.

P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: In developing the recommendations, CGB should consider the success or failure of clean energy recycling approaches used in other jurisdictions, a description of the pros and cons of each approach, and an estimate of each approach’s implementation timeline and cost.

P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: If suggested by CGB as an outcome of these collaborative efforts, the Authority would strongly consider creating a new fee, either applied at the time of project application or on an annual basis per developer, across the state’s clean energy programs to cover the costs associated with solar panel and battery recycling.
P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: Last, the Authority requested that CGB provide an update on the stakeholder process, including any recommendations developed, by August 1, 2024.
P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: Id.

P. SOLAR RECYCLING AND WASTE: Ultimately, while solar panel waste is not yet a prevalent issue in Connecticut, in support of state environmental goals and the Program Objectives, the Authority determines that a solution is needed before the issue becomes commonplace.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: # Disbursement of Funds/Claims Disbursement requests can be made prior to project completion if included in approved application.
Disbursement of Funds/Claims: Most disbursements will occur in one lump sum with the anticipation that project will be commenced and/or completed soon thereafter.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: Recipients may request the lump sum disbursement for less than their loan amount if circumstances have changed including project costs being lower than previously estimated or an increase in matching funds.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: If the recipient fails to request disbursement according to the timeline provided in the application, the recipient must provide an update no less than quarterly to IEDA regarding the deviation from the approved timeline and updates on the plan to implement the project.
Disbursement of Funds/Claims: · Any funds not requested for disbursement within one year of the board approval date may be subject to deobligation and termination of the loan agreement.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: # Reporting Requirements and Monitoring · A startup report is due within 60 days of the later of: the date the project is placed in service/operational or the latest date of all project invoices.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: The report must include, but is not limited to, documentation of project costs and related invoices, one or more photographs, description of unanticipated challenges and lessons learned.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: Utility borrowers will be required to submit annual certifications to confirm that they have maintained their $1.1\times$ debt service coverage ratio, that the revenues generated are adequate to maintain debt service requirements, and are maintaining sufficient unrestricted reserves.
Disbursement of Funds/Claims: Borrowers are expected to engage their financial advisor to complete a pro forma every five years to demonstrate the ability to remain in compliance.

Disbursement of Funds/Claims: A method to ensure compliance with the $1.1\times$ debt service coverage ratio may be a cost of service rate study and adjusting rate structures based on its recommendations.
Staff shall initiate the amendment approval process if the request can be approved without IEC Board approval.
Staff may approve a reduction in award amount and scope no more than 10% lower than the original award amount.
Staff may approve extension of project completion and resulting disbursement schedule no more than one year after the original schedule.

FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: Maryland Energy Administration (MEA): An executive agency of the State of Maryland with a mission to promote clean, affordable, reliable energy and energyrelated greenhouse gas emission reductions to benefit Marylanders in a just and equitable manner.

FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: MEA provides incentives to Maryland residents, businesses, and other Maryland organizations to help pay for clean, efficient, and resilient energy technologies and upgrades.

FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: MEA also advises the Governor and Maryland General Assembly on all energy matters.
FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: MEA is not a private entity.
FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: MEA is an official State of Maryland government agency.

FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: Microgrid: An interconnected system of distributed energy resources (“DERs”) that function together to provide reliable electrical or thermal energy to connected loads in at least two (2) buildings, facilities, or other sites; and is able to rapidly or seamlessly resume operation following a utility power outage, sustain critical loads in the absence of utility power, and is able to rapidly or seamlessly transition back to paralleling with the electric utility following an outage event.

FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: For the purposes of the Resilient Maryland Program, a “Microgrid” differs from a “Resilient Facility Power System” by providing benefits to more than one (1) site.

FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, Area of Interest 1: Preconstruction Planning Funding Opportunity Announcement Appendix 1: Glossary of Terms: Project: A project that is proposed by an applicant to the FY25 Resilient Maryland Program, in accordance with the “Eligible Activities” section of this FOA, and in accordance with COMAR 14.26.02.0217.

Resiliency Hub: A location within a community that is easily accessible and walkable–within a one-half $(	extpercent)$ mile radius–that provides community members with: (1) plug power for personal electronic devices such as cell phones, smartphones, tablets, and laptop computers; (2) plug power for portable medical equipment such as dialysis and continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) machines; (3) refrigeration for temperature-sensitive items; (4) dedicated, safe, healthy conditioned space for community members to locate within; and (5) safe and adequate lighting.

B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: # B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING On June 30, 2021, the Authority established a combined successor program to the state’s Low and Zero Emissions Renewable Energy Credit (LREC/ZREC) and Virtual Net Metering (VNM) programs for non-residential customers, termed the NRES Program.

B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: Decision, June 30, 2021, Docket No. 20-07-01, PURA Implementation of Section 3 of Public Act 19-35, Renewable Energy Tariffs and Procurement Plans (Non-Residential Tariff Decision).
B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: Pursuant to Section III.K.

B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: of the Non-Residential Tariff Decision, the Authority initiates an annual docket to review key Program metrics with stakeholders and to evaluate whether and how the Program should be modified to more fully accomplish the objectives established in the Non-Residential Tariff Decision.
B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: This proceeding serves as the administrative record for the Authority’s review and approval of the Year 3 NRES Program Manual and other key compliance filings.

B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: The Authority conducted the first annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 21- 08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Tariff Program Review – Year 1, issuing a Decision on November 3, 2021 (Year 1 Decision).
B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: The Year 1 Decision finalized the Year 1 Program Manual and set NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2022.

B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: The Authority conducted the second annual NRES Program review in Docket No. 22-08-03, Annual Non-Residential Renewable Energy Solutions Program Review – Year 2, issuing a Decision on November 9, 2022 (Year 2 Decision).

B. BACKGROUND OF THE PROCEEDING: The Decision finalized the Year 2 Program Manual, established NRES Program price caps for project bids received in calendar year 2023, and authorized several changes to the Program’s application requirements to better align the Program with the Program Objectives.
